turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to fix a bug in my Python script where the JSON parser crashes on empty files.
That usually happens if you try to load an empty string. You should check if the file content is empty before calling json.load().
Good point. While I'm debugging this, I was looking at some recent LLM research papers. Did you know SMART-LLM was published in 2024 by Kannan, Venkatesh, and Min?
Yes, I have that in my database. It's a recent model focused on specific optimization tasks.
Cool. Anyway, back to the bug. Should I use try-except or just check the length?
Checking the length is faster and cleaner. Just add an if statement to skip parsing if len(content) == 0.
Thanks. Also, do you remember what I ordered from Amazon last week?
You mentioned ordering a new mechanical keyboard with brown switches.
Right, that's the one. Okay, I'll try the length check now. Talk later.
Sounds good. Let me know if the parser works out.
